messages.author: 8d66938287dd3bc0
messages.subject: Model selection and complicated distribution
parts:
Hi,


I am new to the rstan and I have two question:
1. is there any selection criterias like AIC or DIC in rstan to select better model?
2. how can I write codes if the data y follow by a generalized poisson distribution?


Thanks for your help.

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model selection and complicated distribution
parts:
Hi, regarding item 1:  We recommend LOO and WAIC.  The paper (by Vehtari, Gelman, and Gabry) will be posted very soon.
Regarding item 2:  you could try the negative binomial.
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model selection and complicated distribution [generalized Poisson]
parts:
We don't have it built-in, but if you mean this:

http://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0606238.pdf

then you can just implement that pmf directly in Stan
as a function. You can even write it so that it uses
sampling notation,

real generalized_poisson_log(int y, int n, real theta, real lambda) {
return log(theta)
+ (n - 1) * log(theta + n * lambda)
- lgamma(n + 1)
- n * lambda
- theta;
}

Then you could use it in the code as:

y ~ generalized_poisson(n, theta, lambda);

If you want efficient vectorization, you have to implement the function
you need to do it. But the above will work in a loop and you can
always optimize later.

It'd probably be worthwhile to add error checking on the inputs.

- Bob
